title: How does compound interest work? — Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, Ask CFPB
learningObjectives: Understand that compound interest means earning interest on both the money saved and on the interest already earned
Identify the principal as the amount you start with ($1,000), the interest rate as the percent you earn (5 percent), and the compounding frequency as how often interest is calculated (once a year)
Explain that increasing the compounding frequency, finding a higher interest rate, and adding to the principal help savings grow faster

explanations.text: Compound interest means you earn interest on the money you have saved and also on the interest you have already earned.

evidence.quote: Compound interest is when you earn interest on the money you’ve saved and on the interest you earn along the way.

explanations.text: The source example starts with a principal of $1,000 at an interest rate of 5 percent compounded once a year, resulting in $1,050 after one year and $1,102.50 after two years.

evidence.quote: | Amount you start with | $1,000 | Also called your principal |
| How much you earn | 5 percent | Also called your interest rate, or rate of return |

explanations.text: Savings grow faster when you increase the compounding frequency, seek a higher interest rate, or add to the principal amount.

evidence.quote: | How often you calculate interest | Once a year | Also called your compounding frequency |
Increasing the compounding frequency, finding a higher interest rate, and adding to your principal amount are ways to help your savings grow even faster.
